title: Stable Seedbank & Runner Adapter for Deterministic Profile Publishing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Current profile generation is nondeterministic across harness runners and model variants, leading to flaky perf regressions and noisy published profiles. We need a lightweight, cross-runner seedbank and a deterministic runner adapter that together produce stable, signed profile artifacts for model onboarding and version pinning.

Goals:
- Introduce a Seedbank (content-addressed) that records canonical prompt seeds, sampling parameters, and RNG state for each profile run.
- Implement a Runner Adapter shim (Python + C++ compatible) that accepts a deterministic seed bundle and enforces RNG and sampling semantics across harnesses.
- Publish profile artifacts as manifest-v2 (content-addressed tar + metadata) with deduplication and signature metadata for reproducibility.
- Add lightweight telemetry hooks to capture per-run variance metrics (sample entropy, latency quantiles, token distributions) to attach to profiles for downstream QA and rollouts.

Design constraints and decisions:
- Use a compact seed format: sha256(prompt + normalized-params + stable-order-tags) -> seed-id. Keeps artifacts small and facilitates dedupe.
- Runner adapter will expose a minimal API: run_with_seed(seed-id, model_version, runner_flags) so older harnesses can be shimmed with ~2 lines.
- Do not change core model sampling kernels; adapter must configure RNG and sampling boundary checks only. This avoids touching performance-critical code paths.
- Profile manifest-v2 will include: seed-ids, model-version pin, runner-version, kernel-hints, telemetry-summary, CI-golden-hash, and optional signer.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end run generates identical profile-summary.json across 3 different runner implementations (python-harness, cc-fast-harness, rust-proxy) for the same seed-id and model-version.
2) Published manifest-v2 artifacts are content-addressed and deduplicated in the artifact store.
3) CI gating job rejects profile publishes if sample-variance > configured threshold or if golden-hash mismatches.
4) Documentation and shim examples added to the harness repo and onboarding playbook.

Out of scope:
- Changing internal model kernels.
- Full cryptographic signing HSM integration (we will add signer metadata; HSM later).
